title: Polish Thorn declaration: sins against conscience forfeit justifying grace for a time
source_text: XX. Poloni vero Theologi in declaratione suae sententiae, in colloquio Thoruniensi oblata, expresse docent renatos, quoties in peccata contra conscientiam recidunt, in iisque aliquandiu perseverant, nec gratiam justificantem, nec Spiritum Sanctum, pro illo tempore retinere; sed novum irae ac mortis aeternae reatum incurrere: cum res secus se habeat, quando non peccant contra conscientiam, sed ex infirmitate & inadvertentia. Etenim haec sunt eorum verba, Falso accusamur quasi statuamus semel justificatos Dei gratiam, ejusve certitudinem, & ipsum Spiritum Sanctum non posse amittere, quamvis in peccatis pro lubitu volutentur. Cum contra potius doceamus ipsos etiam renatos, quoties in peccata contra conscientiam recidunt, in iisque aliquandiu perseverant, nec fidem veram, nec Dei gratiam justificantem, nedum ejus certitudinem, aut Spiritum Sanctum pro tempore illo retinere; sed novum irae ac mortis aeternae reatum incurrere: ac propterea, nisi speciali Dei gratia excitante (quod in electis fieri non dubitamus) ad resipiscentiam serum renoventur, reipsa etiam damnandos esse. Titulo de Gratia, sect. 2. num. 11.
pass_a_gloss: But the Polish theologians in the declaration of their opinion offered at the Colloquy of Thorn expressly teach that the regenerate, as often as they relapse into sins against conscience and persevere in them for some time, retain for that time neither justifying grace nor the Holy Spirit; but incur a new guilt of wrath and eternal death: whereas the matter stands otherwise when they do not sin against conscience but from infirmity and inadvertence. For these are their words: We are falsely accused as if we held that those once justified cannot lose God’s grace or the certainty of it and the Holy Spirit himself, although they wallow in sins at pleasure. Whereas on the contrary we rather teach that even the regenerate themselves, as often as they relapse into sins against conscience and persevere in them for some time, retain for that time neither true faith nor God’s justifying grace, much less the certainty of it, or the Holy Spirit; but incur a new guilt of wrath and eternal death: and therefore, unless by God’s special exciting grace (which we do not doubt happens in the elect) they are renewed late unto repentance, they are even in very deed to be damned. Under the title On Grace, section 2, number 11.
pass_b_english: At Thorn the Poles deny once-justified antinomian security: conscience-wounding relapse forfeits justifying grace and the Spirit for that time.
Infirmity-slips differ; without special exciting grace unto late repentance such falls leave the sinner damnable in deed.
